description: Hi! We're a team of two turning NASA data into real-world impact. 🚀 We bring product vision, design, storytelling, and business strategy. We're tackling Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data, building a dashboard that helps farmers choose climate-smart crops.
summary: GroundTwin is an interactive planetary analog platform and radar-calibration tool designed to help space agencies identify the best Earth testbeds for future lunar south-pole bases and Mars landing sites. Our solution addresses the challenge through two paths. First, we standardize and combine eight multi-agency satellite datasets (covering geology, terrain, temperature, water, dust, habitability, subsurface features, and mission safety) into a transparent similarity map. After validating our model on established NASA testbeds like the Atacama Desert and Devon Island, we discovered a promising new Martian analog in Mangystau, Kazakhstan—ranking in the top 9.5% of Earth’s land for Gale Crater and top 8.3% for Jezero. Second, we calibrate orbital radar on real Earth surfaces and merge Mini-RF, LOLA, and Diviner (<110 K) data to rank the top 10 lunar south-pole craters for viable water ice. By pairing transparent criteria with honest physical limits (such as gravity and radiation differences), GroundTwin enables safer, cost-effective mission testing before launch.
details:
What It Does & How It Works GroundTwin is an interactive planetary analog platform and orbital radar calibration system designed to identify Earth testbeds for future lunar south-pole bases and Mars landing sites. It operates through two integrated paths:

  1. Earth & Mars/Moon Analogs (8 Standardized Criteria): We normalize and combine multi-agency satellite datasets across eight mission-critical dimensions—Geology & Mineralogy, Topography & Terrain, Temperature & Illumination, Water & Resources, Dust & Surface Processes, Biology & Habitability, Subsurface Features, and Mission Operations & Safety. Users can adjust criterion weights by mission profile (science, rover testing, or habitat construction) to explore transparent, grid-by-grid similarity scores ($0.5^\circ$ resolution) rather than opaque black-box percentages.
  2. Lunar Water-Ice Screening (Radar Calibration + 3/3 Criteria): Because rough rocks can mimic ice in orbital radar returns, we first calibrated synthetic aperture radar (SAR) backscatter on real Earth surfaces (smooth ground < rough rocks < water ice). We then cross-referenced three lunar south-pole datasets—Mini-RF radar, LOLA terrain roughness/slope, and Diviner surface temperatures (<110 K)—to rank the Top-10 south-pole craters by full (3/3) and partial (2/3) ice clues.

Benefits, Impact & Key Discovery Field expeditions to Antarctica or remote testbeds are costly and logistically complex. GroundTwin enables mission planners to pre-screen accessible Earth analogs and understand why a site matches. After validating our scoring formula against established NASA benchmarks (Atacama Desert, Utah MDRS, and Devon Island), we identified a major new Martian analog in Mangystau, Kazakhstan—the vanished floor of the ancient Tethys Sea, featuring layered sedimentary cliffs (Bozjyra) and evaporite salt flats (Tuzbair) that rank in the top 9.5% of Earth’s land for Gale Crater and top 8.3% for Jezero.

Tools, Data & Software Used

  • Programming & Data Analysis: Python (NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Rasterio) for geospatial normalization, multi-criteria similarity scoring, and radar backscatter calibration; LaTeX for our technical research paper.
  • Open Space Agency Datasets: NASA Earthdata / Worldview (MODIS, GPM, ASTER GDEM), NASA PDS (LRO Mini-RF, LOLA, Diviner), USGS (GMTED2010), Canadian Space Agency (RCM / RADARSAT), Copernicus / ESA, and JAXA G-Portal.
  • Web Platform & Visualization: Framer, interactive 3D Earth/Moon globe visualizations, and custom UI components hosted on GitHub Pages and Framer.

Creativity & Factors Considered Rather than treating similarity as a single unexplainable percentage, we introduced mission-specific weight presets, a radar calibration bridge between Earth glaciers and lunar craters, and a dedicated "What Earth Cannot Reproduce" honesty block on every analog profile—explicitly accounting for reduced gravity ($1/6g$ and $0.38g$), vacuum/thin atmosphere, cosmic radiation, and the physical necessity of drilling to confirm lunar ice with 100% certainty
